L153: # Terms of Use for arXiv APIs
L154: Our mission is to provide rapid dissemination of scientific results at no cost to authors or readers. Providing free Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) helps us to advance that mission by enabling platforms and projects that extend the discoverability of arXiv e-prints and provide valuable services to scientists and interested readers. Our APIs include our 【88†OAI-PMH interface】, 【47†RSS feeds】, the 【59†legacy arXiv API】, 【58†bulk data downloads】, and 【89†SWORD bulk deposit API】.
L155: Understanding and observing the following terms of use will help us to ensure that arXiv continues to be able to fulfill its mission.
L156: By using arXiv APIs, you are agreeing to the terms and conditions outlined on this page.
L157:   * You understand that e-prints from arXiv are subject to all applicable copyright protections. The redistribution of e-prints requires permission from the copyright holder, which may be the author(s) or publisher. arXiv is not the copyright holder on any of the e-prints available through the API. In some cases, submitters have provided permission in advance by submitting their e-print under a permissive Creative Commons license.
L158: The vast majority of e-prints are submitted under the 【90†arXiv.org non-exclusive right to distribute†arxiv.org】. For more information about licenses, see https://arxiv.org/help/license.
L159:   * You are free to use descriptive 【91†metadata†arxiv.org】^{1} about arXiv e-prints under the terms of the 【92†Creative Commons Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Declaration†creativecommons.org】. Metadata are provided by authors, volunteer moderators, arXiv staff, and external partners.
L160:   * You agree to abide by the arXiv 【75†Code of Conduct】 in all of your interactions with arXiv staff and those involved in its operation, and understand that if you violate the CoC we may prohibit you from using arXiv APIs.
L161:   * You agree to respect limitations on use of arXiv APIs, including rate limits and authorization mechanisms. If we think that you are attempting to circumvent those limitations, that your use of arXiv APIs threatens normal operation or availability of the arXiv platform, or that you are doing something illegal or unethical, we may further limit or block your access.
L162:   * You understand that we will make changes to arXiv APIs that may lead to compatibility issues with your code. We will do our best to provide advance notice of such changes via our 【93†website†arxiv.org】 under arXiv News and the 【94†arXiv API group†groups.google.com】. It is up to you to keep track of changes that might affect your use of arXiv APIs and to make any required changes.
L163:   * In order to provide support and improvements for developers who use arXiv APIs, you understand that we will collect certain private information about you, such as your name and email address. Please see the 【76†arXiv Privacy Policy】 for information about how we use and protect your information. In order to promote use of arXiv APIs and showcase your work, we may give you the option to make information about you or your project publicly available.
L164: ## Limitations
L165: ### Rate limits
L166: 
L167: Please note that the following rate limits apply to all of the machines under your control as a whole. You should not attempt to overcome these limits by increasing the number of machines used to make requests. If your use-case requires a higher request rate, please 【95†contact our support team†arxiv.org】.
L168: 
L169:   * When using the legacy APIs (including OAI-PMH, RSS, and the arXiv API), make no more than one request every three seconds, and limit requests to a single connection at a time.
L170: These limits may change in the future.
L171: ## Things that you can (and should!) do
L172:   * Retrieve, store, transform, and share descriptive metadata about arXiv e-prints.
L173:   * Retrieve, store, and use the content of arXiv e-prints for your own personal use, or for research purposes.
L174:   * Provide tools and services to users that helps them to discover or be notified about arXiv e-prints. For example:
L175:   * A better search interface;
L176:   * A mobile app that notifies users about e-prints that might be of interest to them;
L177:   * A visualization of topics in arXiv e-prints over time;
L178:   * A citation graph using bibliographic references from e-prints.
L179:   * Build other kinds of interfaces that help users to interact with arXiv in new and useful ways, leveraging our APIs.
L180:   * Direct users to arXiv.org to retrieve e-print content (PDF, source files, etc). We encourage you to link to the abstract page.
L181: ## Things that you must not do
L182:   * Store and serve arXiv e-prints (PDFs, source files, or other content) from your servers, unless you have the permission of the copyright holder or are permitted to do so by the license with which the e-print was submitted. Note that a very small subset of arXiv e-prints are submitted with licenses that permit redistribution.
L183:   * Represent your project as endorsed or supported by arXiv.org without our permission.
L184:   * Attempt to circumvent rate limits.

L14: # The REST API for OpenCitations Index
L15: 
L16: Version: Version 2.2.0 (2025-04-15)
L17: API URL: 【10†https://api.opencitations.net/index/v2】
L18: Contact: contact@opencitations.net
L19: License: This document is licensed with a 【11†Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License†creativecommons.org】, while the REST API itself has been created using 【12†RAMOSE†github.com】, the Restful API Manager Over SPARQL Endpoints created by 【13†Silvio Peroni†orcid.org】, which is licensed with an 【14†ISC license†opensource.org】.
L20: ## Description 【15†back to top】
L21: This document describe the REST API for accessing the data stored in the 【16†OpenCitations Index†w3id.org】 hosted by 【17†OpenCitations†opencitations.net】.
L22: This API implements operations to retrieve the citation data for all the references to other works appearing in a particular bibliographic entity, or the citation data for all the references appearing in other works to a particular bibliographic entity, given the identifier of a bibliographic entity, or to retrieve citation data about a particular citation identified by means of its 【18†Open Citation Identifier (OCI)†opencitations.wordpress.com】.
L23: All the present operations return either a JSON document (default) or a CSV document according to the mimetype specified in the `Accept` header of the request. If you would like to suggest an additional operation to be included in this API, please use the 【19†issue tracker†github.com】 of the OpenCitations APIs available on GitHub.
L24: `API calls are rate-limited to 180 requests/minute per IP address` to ensure fair usage and service availability. For large-scale data retrieval, please use the database dumps available at 【20†download.opencitations.net†download.opencitations.net】.
L25: If you are going to use the REST APIs within an application/code, we encourage you to get the 【21†OpenCitations Access Token†opencitations.net】 and specify it in the "authorization" header of your REST API call. Here is a usage example in Python:
L26: 
L27:     `
L28:     from requests import get
L29: 
L30:     API_CALL = "https://api.opencitations.net/index/v2/references/doi:10.1186/1756-8722-6-59"
L31:     HTTP_HEADERS = {"authorization": "YOUR-OPENCITATIONS-ACCESS-TOKEN"}
L32: 
L33:     get(API_CALL, headers=HTTP_HEADERS)
L34:     `
L35: ## Parameters 【15†back to top】
L36: 
L37: Parameters can be used to filter and control the results returned by the API. They are passed as normal HTTP parameters in the URL of the call. They are:
L38: 
L39:   1. `require=<field_name>`: all the rows that have an empty value in the `<field_name>` specified are removed from the result set - e.g. `require=given_name` removes all the rows that do not have any string specified in the `given_name` field.
L40:   2. `filter=<field_name>:<operator><value>`: only the rows compliant with `<value>` are kept in the result set. The parameter `<operation>` is not mandatory. If `<operation>` is not specified, `<value>` is interpreted as a regular expression, otherwise it is compared by means of the specified operation. Possible operators are "=", "<", and ">".
L41: For instance, `filter=title:semantics?` returns all the rows that contain the string "semantic" or "semantics" in the field `title`, while `filter=date:>2016-05` returns all the rows that have a `date` greater than May 2016.
L42:   3. `sort=<order>(<field_name>)`: sort in ascending (`<order>` set to "asc") or descending (`<order>` set to "desc") order the rows in the result set according to the values in `<field_name>`. For instance, `sort=desc(date)` sorts all the rows according to the value specified in the field `date` in descending order.
L43:   4. `format=<format_type>`: the final table is returned in the format specified in `<format_type>` that can be either "csv" or "json" - e.g. `format=csv` returns the final table in CSV format. This parameter has higher priority of the type specified through the "Accept" header of the request. Thus, if the header of a request to the API specifies `Accept: text/csv` and the URL of such request includes `format=json`, the final table is returned in JSON.
L44:   5. `json=<operation_type>("<separator>",<field>,<new_field_1>,<new_field_2>,...)`: in case a JSON format is requested in return, tranform each row of the final JSON table according to the rule specified. If `<operation_type>` is set to "array", the string value associated to the field name `<field>` is converted into an array by splitting the various textual parts by means of `<separator>`. For instance, considering the JSON table `[ { "names": "Doe, John; Doe, Jane" }, ...
L45: ]`, the execution of `array("; ",names)` returns `[ { "names": [ "Doe, John", "Doe, Jane" ], ... ]`. Instead, if `<operation_type>` is set to "dict", the string value associated to the field name `<field>` is converted into a dictionary by splitting the various textual parts by means of `<separator>` and by associating the new fields `<new_field_1>`, `<new_field_2>`, etc., to these new parts. For instance, considering the JSON table `[ { "name": "Doe, John" }, ...
L46: ]`, the execution of `dict(", ",name,fname,gname)` returns `[ { "name": { "fname": "Doe", "gname": "John" }, ... ]`.
L47: It is possible to specify one or more filtering operation of the same kind (e.g. `require=given_name&require=family_name`). In addition, these filtering operations are applied in the order presented above - first all the `require` operation, then all the `filter` operations followed by all the `sort` operation, and finally the `format` and the `json` operation (if applicable).
L48: It is worth mentioning that each of the aforementioned rules is applied in order, and it works on the structure returned after the execution of the previous rule.
L49: Example: `<api_operation_url>?require=doi&filter=date:>2015&sort=desc(date)`.
L50: ## Operations 【15†back to top】
L51: 
L52: The operations that this API implements are:
L53:   * 【3†/citation/{oci}】: This operation retrieves the citation metadata for the citation identified by the input Open Citation Identifier (OCI).
L54:   * 【4†/citation-count/{id}】: This operation retrieves the number of incoming citations to the bibliographic entity identified by the input PID (DOI, PMID, ISSN, ISBN, OMID)..
L55:   * 【5†/venue-citation-count/{id}】: This operation retrieves the number of incoming citations to all the bibliographic entities published into aspecific journal identified by the input ISSN.
L56:   * 【6†/reference-count/{id}】: This operation retrieves the number of outgoing citations from the bibliographic entity identified by the input PID (DOI, PMID, ISSN, ISBN, OMID).
L57:   * 【7†/citations/{id}】: This operation retrieves the citation data for all the references appearing in the reference lists of other citing works to the bibliographic entity identified by the input PID (DOI, PMID, ISSN, ISBN, OMID), that constitute the incoming citations of that identified bibliographic entity.
L58:   * 【8†/references/{id}】: This operation retrieves the citation data for all the outgoing references to other cited works appearing in the reference list of the bibliographic entity identified by the input PID (DOI, PMID, ISSN, ISBN, OMID)..
L59: ### /citation/{oci} 【2†back to operations】
L60: 
L61: This operation retrieves the citation metadata for the citation identified by the input Open Citation Identifier (OCI).
L62: 
L63: The Open Citation Identifier is a globally unique persistent identifier for bibliographic citations, which has a simple structure: the lower-case letters "oci" followed by a colon, followed by two numbers separated by a dash. For example, `oci:1-18` is a valid OCI.
L64: It is worth mentioning that, in this REST operation, the prefix "oci:" should not be specified, and only the dash-separated numbers of the OCI should be provided, as shown in the example below.
L65: 
L66: The fields returned by this operation are:
L67:   * oci: the Open Citation Identifier (OCI) of the citation in consideration;
L68:   * citing: the PIDs of the citing entity;
L69:   * cited: the PIDs of the cited entity;
L70:   * creation: the creation date of the citation according to the 【22†ISO date format†en.wikipedia.org】 `YYYY-MM-DD`, which corresponds to the publication date of the citing entity;
L71:   * timespan: the interval between the publication date of the cited entity and the publication date of the citing entity, expressed using the 【23†XSD duration format†www.w3.org】 `PnYnMnD`;
L72:   * journal_sc: it records whether the citation is a journal self-citations (i.e. the citing and the cited entities are published in the same journal);
